author: Tardigraph / Meow-Ludo; Gross, Müller, Hehn, Ferstl, Allner, Dierolf, Achterhold, Mayer and Pfeiffer (2019)
basis_label: Nano-CT specimen and 152 µm body-length definition
note: Native-micrometre nano-CT reconstruction of one fixed, dried Hypsibius exemplaris from Gross et al. (2019), via Tardigraph’s organ meshes and CT-traced body surface. The published 152 µm body length excludes the fourth leg pair; those legs remain in the mesh. The dorsal/front shell quarter is removed to expose original whole-body organ segmentations, with false colours. The independently registered head scan is omitted; labels identified as probable by Tardigraph remain interpretive. Drying shrinkage and resolution limit fine detail; this is one small specimen, not a species-wide standard. Dataset integration must use the 152 µm specimen definition.

operations: Retain whole-body scan structures and CT-derived external tracing
Omit independently registered higher-resolution head scan
Remove dorsal/front quarter of external shell for inspection; retain organs at original positions
Simplify each structure; recompute normals; no coordinate scaling
